name_note: The GTDB genus g__Pilosibacter corresponds to the genus Pilosibacter, whose described species include Pilosibacter fragilis and Pilosibacter rotomagensis; many catalog genomes carry older Clostridium names.

sentences.text: Pilosibacter is a genus of Gram-positive, obligately anaerobic bacteria proposed for strains isolated from the faeces of healthy people.
Pilosibacter fragilis was initially placed in the family Clostridiaceae, and a later study proposed transferring the genus Pilosibacter to the family Lachnospiraceae.
A strain described as the species Pilosibacter rotomagensis was isolated from the gut microbiota of healthy individuals and reported to be a potent butyrate producer.
That strain is described as anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive, non-motile and non-spore-forming, with optimal growth reported at 37 degrees Celsius and pH between 5.7 and 7.0.
